items.mathematical_definition_draft: A subset U⊆X is retrocompact in X if the inclusion U→X is quasi-compact; equivalently, U∩V is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open subset V⊆X. Here U is additionally assumed open.

items.scope_and_edge_case: A retrocompact open U need not be quasi-compact as an abstract space when X itself is not quasi-compact; if X is quasi-compact, taking V=X forces U quasi-compact.
items.semantic_integration_note: Retain relative retrocompactness versus absolute quasi-compactness; do not invent a Hausdorff assumption.

items.mathematical_definition_draft: For any proposition P, its Iverson bracket [P] is 1 if P is true and 0 if P is false; this is the indicator of the truth set of P.

items.semantic_integration_note: General Iverson notation specializes to [a=b], but must not be conflated with equality-specific Kronecker delta.

items.mathematical_definition_draft: A binary relation R on S is antisymmetric if for all x,y∈S, (x,y)∈R and (y,x)∈R together imply x=y.

items.scope_and_edge_case: Does not require comparability or reflexivity. Unlike asymmetry, an antisymmetric relation may include all diagonal pairs.

items.mathematical_definition_draft: Let C_ℚ be the ring of rational Cauchy sequences and ∼ identify sequences whose difference converges to zero. The canonical map ℚ→C_ℚ/∼ sends q to the class of constant sequence (q,q,…); it respects + and × and is injective.

external_source_evidence.relevance: Standard construction lead; exact passage and quotient equivalence need verification.

items.scope_and_edge_case: Well-defined field embedding depends on proof that null Cauchy sequences form an ideal and that every nonzero class has multiplicative inverse; kernel of constant-sequence map is zero.
items.semantic_integration_note: Retain distinction from principal Dedekind cut embedding (priority 312), even though resulting reals are isomorphic.

original_provenance.original_context: Graph theory: neighborhood N_G(v)={u∈V:{u,v}∈E} in a simple undirected graph G=(V,E).

items.mathematical_definition_draft: In a simple undirected graph G=(V,E) with E⊆{{u,v}:u,v∈V,u≠v}, the (open) neighbor set of vertex v is N_G(v)={u∈V:{u,v}∈E}.

external_source_evidence.relevance: Directly checked N(v) consists of vertices adjacent to v, excluding v; separately notes closed N[v]=N(v)∪{v}.

items.scope_and_edge_case: No loops allowed, hence v∉N_G(v); closed neighborhood includes v and differs. For directed graphs distinguish in/out neighbors.
items.semantic_integration_note: Do not equate vertex degree with neighbor set itself, though |N_G(v)|=deg(v) for simple undirected graphs.
items.source_audit_note: Replaces ambiguous generic Neighborhood.html: that source describes graph neighborhoods commonly INCLUDING the vertex, incompatible with this candidate's open N_G(v) convention.
